newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Uneasy calm in Bangui after African force in clash.
newsitem.headline: Uneasy calm in Bangui after African force in clash.

text.p: An uneasy calm reigned in the capital of the Central African Republic on Saturday, one day after a Senegalese soldier and a child were killed in a clash between African peacekeepers and disaffected soldiers.

A spokesman for the soldiers, many of whom have already rejoined their units under a January 25 peace deal to end three army mutinies in under a year, told Reuters they had told their men not to attack but to remain on the defensive.

A spokesman for the peacekeepers told of contacts between the two sides but said no formal meeting had yet been organised. An isolated explosion, possibly from a Rocket Propelled Grenade, rocked their positions on Saturday but caused no damage.
The Red Cross said the soldier was shot dead in Friday's clashes and a boy aged 12 had been killed by an explosion. He said eight other people had been wounded, one seriously.
Friday's incident was the first since a failed June 13 attempt to reintegrate mutineers from the paramilitary gendarmerie into their units under the January peace plan.
Mali's widely respected former military leader, Amadou Toumani Toure, who brokered the January deal, was expected back in Bangui on Saturday.

The first mutinies, in April and May 1996, began as protests over pay but became a movement to topple President Ange-Felix Patasse, a northern civilian elected in 1993. The third mutiny began in November and degenerated into ethnic bloodshed.
